answer: The onyx lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the shale is where a second reviewer recomputes them. The nadir of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, released only after three unrelated confirmations, no identity may audit its own recruit.
